name: The Flavor Archive: Cuisine, Loss, and the Synthesis Century
description: An intimate and melancholy neural-feed documentary exploring the near-total replacement of traditional food cultures with synthesized nutrition across all tiers of GLMZ, told through the testimonies of the last practitioners of heritage cooking, food memory specialists, and the children of immigrants who can no longer access the ingredients their grandparents used. The neural-feed format was chosen deliberately to let viewers taste reconstructed flavors from oral descriptions and fragmentary chemical records — a process the film calls 'flavor archaeology.' Director Saoirse Nwosu-Bergström spent five years collecting taste-memory testimonies from Shelf communities before the last living practitioners died.
cultural_impact: The film's release coincided with a surge in illegal heritage ingredient markets and is credited with making 'flavor archaeology' a recognized cultural preservation discipline.
story_hooks: One of the film's reconstructed flavor sequences triggers a violent memory in a Shelf viewer whose BCI carries suppressed trauma from a forced relocation — the flavor was from a specific neighborhood that no longer exists.
NutriCorp's legal delay of the film's certification turns out to have been covering the time needed to acquire and demolish the last urban community garden in the Outer Stack.
A Spire-tier food executive secretly funded part of the film's production and their motives — collecting taste-memory data for a luxury synthesis product — are discovered mid-distribution.
